beats.headline: You are not seeing the magistrate
beats.text: Two of them at my desk. A human with no shoes, a cat that talks, and a body. They have put a body on my desk. Evidence, they call it, and the human has shown the swordsmen a pass for it from the magistrate, so they leave without him. The magistrate is not to be disturbed. If he does not care about your business then he will certainly care about being disturbed, and I will not be discussing it further. Behind me is a shelf of beanbag figures in their proper order, and the human is standing far too close to it. The door behind me is locked. It is locked for a reason.

beats.headline: Dynamite in the shelves
beats.text: They did not come back. They did not need to. The human fixed my shelf for me, the day he threw a dead woman across my desk, while I was on the floor gathering my figures, and I did not so much as look up. The shelves are hollow. Three sticks of hobgoblin dynamite and a detonator are sitting inside the second one now, under my figures, which is the one place nobody ever looks, because nobody but me has ever cared what stands on that shelf.

beats.headline: The administrative building, and everything in it
beats.text: Miss Quill is dead. The reception office came apart with her in it, and the shelf, and every figure on it. Magistrate Featherfall, credited dead in the same blast, had been hanging mummified in a dreamcatcher of bone in the rooms behind for a long time before any of this. The barefoot man is magistrate of this settlement now, which is what happens when nobody checks the paperwork. He collects one achievement for assassinating a public official and a second for killing an NPC another crawler needed for a quest. The achievement declines to say whose, or what the quest was. She kept that door for a very long time and not one crawler ever thought to ask her why.

beats.headline: Correction to the file
beats.text: Remex tells them the rest of it, there being nobody left to stop him. She was not guarding the magistrate. She was guarding what she had done to her own husband: let Featherfall drag him back into the world as a soul leech, knowing the feedback would kill Featherfall, and kept him above the swordsmen's warehouse as her capacitor, feeding off the soul crystal, so that she would have the mana for a working called The Final War. The devotion to the figures was real. The refusals at that desk were real. Both of them were also the cover, and I filed her as an obstructive minor official for the whole of the season.
